environment.build: Rust dev/test with local Qt 6.11.2 toolchain
environment.scope: Pure Rust logical-key policy model; no native key routing changed

observations: All 130 core tests pass, including the Mixed token parser, exact global/profile/site/runtime layering, whole-list replacement, explicit empty-list clearing, duplicate and 64-entry limits, reserved controls, unknown syntax, and atomic errors.
Logical case, existing named modifier tokens, one-grapheme Unicode text, and the four UTF-16-unit text limit are preserved; AltGr spellings are not aliased to Ctrl+Alt tokens.
The Rust token parser accepts every named token emitted by KeyboardPresentation.logicalNormalKeyText and Alt+1 through Alt+9; AltGr+p remains an unknown token.
An idle mapped g or digit is page-owned; an active browser count or keychain remains browser-owned through continuation.

A keychain mismatch is consumed, timeout clears its prefix without output, and resetting an incomplete resolver for a policy revision emits no buffered key to the page. A later fresh gesture is classified under the effective policy.
